headline: Revenue up 161% to $14.6B, net income of $4.4B
summary: SpaceX revenue rose 161% to $14.6B in Q3 2026 and net income was $4.4B, against a $1.1B loss a year earlier, while adjusted EBITDA rose 306% to $8.8B. The Super Intelligence (AI) segment brought in $7.6B and Starlink consumer subscribers reached 13.6 million.
points: Starship Flight 14, its first orbital flight and first revenue-generating mission, delivered 26 Starlink V3 satellites, about 10 times the downlink capacity added by a Falcon 9 Starlink launch.
AI revenue growth came from new cloud services agreements, the Cursor acquisition (completed 14 August, adding $608M of revenue) and wider Grok adoption.
Of the $19.6B capital spending, $16.4B went to the AI segment as the COLOSSUS II compute buildout continued.
Completed 35 launches in the quarter, 12 for customers, and signed three more NASA ISS crew missions and 18 National Security Space Launch missions.
Agreed on 8 October to buy 800 MHz spectrum licences for Starlink Mobile, expected to close in the first half of 2027.
guidance: The results release gave no numerical outlook. Reuters reported that SpaceX expects capital spending to stay near the third-quarter level of $19.6B in the near future.
reaction: Shares were up 2.5% in extended trading on 20 October, according to Reuters at about 17:40 ET (22:40 UK time); CNBC reported a gain of about 5% in extended trading.
